label: rejected

evidence.V1: Stacked faceted strata with a mossy cap read as a cliff/rock chunk in front and three-quarter; silhouette shows distinct stepped ledges; bottom-origin and seated (all strata seated, no gaps).
evidence.V2: Big strata slabs and medium designed facets are clear, but there is almost no small tier: the only secondary read is the moss top, with no chips, cracks or pebbles.
evidence.V3: Slab stack is partly stylised, but the second stratum is sunk into the one below (0.26 stud penetration) leaving a thin sliver lip and a wedge-shaped dark slit that looks accidental rather than designed; strata are similar thickness so the stack reads a bit uniform.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistently softened edges that catch light across all strata.
evidence.V5: Strata close-up (flat and studio) shows a thin wedge/sliver where stratum 2 intersects stratum 1, reading as a pinched crevice; otherwise facets shade cleanly.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values plus a single leaf-green moss secondary; colourways (sandstone, redrock) keep the structure.
evidence.V7: 538 tris vs medium target 2000 (ceiling 4000): well under target.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, designed rock facets, stone hue + moss green secondary per the Nature kit; moss green is slightly saturated but within the scheme.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Hull (Box per stratum option), CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, bottom-centre origin.

evidence.V1: Silhouette and front/three-quarter read as a stacked, overhanging rock chunk from every angle (step notch under the mossy cap slab and undercut base both show in the outline); top reads as a moss-capped rock.
evidence.V2: Big (four strata slabs) and medium (flat facets) are clear, but there is no small tier: no cracks, chips, pebbles or moss fringe, so the read stops at slab level.
evidence.V3: Strata are four similar-thickness lens-shaped pancakes stacked with modest offsets; it reads as a stacked cairn more than a confident chunky cliff, so it is only partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Consistent narrow chamfers on all facet edges catch the studio light (close_strata_studio, close_top_studio), and the moss cap edge is also softened.
evidence.V5: Mostly clean flat facets, but the second stratum sits in a dished top with a dark sliver wedge and a creased fold where it meets the slab below (close_strata_flat), plus 116 cross-shell overlaps; a minor artifact, not a broken surface.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one stone hue in 2-3 grey values plus moss green secondary; colourways (basalt, sandstone) keep the same two-material scheme.
evidence.V7: 538 tris against a medium target of 2000 (ceiling 4000).
evidence.V8: Designed flat facets with chamfers, one vertex-colour material, stone hue + leaf-green secondary as the Nature kit specifies.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for static scenery: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, white MeshPart.Color with vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Stacked-strata cliff chunk reads from front, three-quarter and top; silhouette shows a clear layered stack with overhangs.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: 4 strata slabs (big), moss-capped top slab and stepped overhangs (medium), designed facet breaks (small).
evidence.V3: Layered slab idea is stylised, but the bottom slab is pushed out forward-left and tilted like a separate fallen plate, and the second stratum reads as a thin dish sunk into the one below, so the stack feels loose rather than one confident cliff mass.
evidence.V4: Facets carry consistent soft highlight bevels on all strata ridges (close_strata_studio); no razor edges.
evidence.V5: close_strata studio/flat show a dark wedge-shaped sliver where the thin second stratum cuts into the larger slab (stratum2 penetration 0.257, 116 cross-shell overlaps) - reads as a pinched crease, a visible artifact.
evidence.V6: Stone grey in 3 values + one moss green cap; redrock and slate colourways hold the same scheme.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material, stone hue + moss secondary, designed flat facets with soft normals: matches Nature kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull (or Box per stratum), CanTouch off, CastShadow on, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre; all gates pass.

artifacts: Wedge-shaped sliver / slit where stratum 2 is sunk into stratum 1 (front strata close-up)
Creased fold / dark sliver wedge where stratum 2 sinks into the dished top of stratum 1 (close_strata views)
116 cross-shell overlaps between strata (intentional interpenetration, but stratum 2 penetration 0.26 studs is deep)
Thin second stratum intersects the slab beneath it, producing a dark wedge/sliver crease visible in close_strata studio and flat renders
Bottom stratum offset and tilted outward so it reads like a detached plate
top_fixes: Re-seat stratum 2 so it rests on stratum 1 with a clean overhang instead of sinking in and leaving a thin sliver/slit
Vary strata thickness and add a small tier (chipped corners, a crack line, a pebble or moss drip down one face)
Let the moss spill a little over the top edge so it reads as growth rather than a painted cap
Rework stratum 2 so it sits on a flat ledge instead of sinking into a dished slab, removing the crease and sliver wedge
Vary strata thickness and offsets more (a thick base block, thin ledges) so it reads as a cliff chunk rather than stacked pancakes
Add a small detail tier: a few cracks or chipped corners and a moss fringe dripping over the cap edge
Widen the value spread between strata (slightly darker lower strata) for depth
Reduce stratum2 penetration / thicken it so it rests on top of stratum1 instead of slicing into it (remove the wedge crease)
Pull the bottom slab back under the stack and level it so the chunk reads as one cliff mass
Vary strata thickness more deliberately (thicker base, thinner top) for a stronger stylised read
